reason: A measure (PATO_0001334 diameter) used as the yardstick of a ratio ('0.5-1 x their own diameter', '1-3 diameters apart'), not a structure. The part being described is the scale or the centre. These are pattern 10 ratios whose second term is a dimension of the bearer itself or of its neighbours.

A ratio fragment ('2-3 x as long as tube'): the tube is the second term of a pattern 10 comparison, and the part described is the lobe or limb. The tube itself would be the corolla tube (FLOPO_0985018), calyx tube (FLOPO_0986011) or perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010), depending on the sentence. Same treatment as 'lip length' and 'pedicel length'.

The second term of a pattern 10 ratio ('filaments ca. 1/4 anther length', 'apiculum 1/3-1/2 the length of the anther'). The part described is the filament or apiculum; the anther (PO_0009066) is only the comparison term. Same as the rejected 'lip length'.
Narrower: culm is a synonym of stem (PO_0009047), and a culm node is a stem node of a grass or sedge. Pilose, glabrous, sericeous and prominent are qualities of the node.

target: labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) with has position median (FLOPO_0991381), pattern 18
reason: A position in the series of labellum lobes. This parallels the earlier 'lateral lobe of the labellum', which mapped to labellum lobe with lateral (FLOPO_0991380). 'Apex truncate' gives the apex region of this bearer (pattern 12 with plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023).

Bare 'rachis' was rejected as generic (2026-11-13), and the margin does not settle which rachis. In the grass floras (Paspalum: margins scabrous, incurved, green, winged racemes) it is plant organ margin (PO_0025005) of the inflorescence axis (PO_0020122). In fern and compound-leaf floras it is the margin of the leaf rachis (PO_0020055). Allow it only per flora or family, or as 'rachis' within a named inflorescence.

target: extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057) part of cyathium (FLOPO_0985029), pattern 12 (bearer_container FLOPO_0985029)
reason: Narrower. The glands on the rim of the Euphorbia cyathium involucre are nectaries outside the flowers, because the cyathium is an inflorescence. The cyathium class exists, so a container rule expresses them without a new term. Colour and shape (transversely ovate, rounded to truncate) are qualities of the gland. Their petaloid appendages are a separate part.

target: petal base (PO_0025146) part of orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978), bearer_container FLOPO_0980978
reason: Narrower. The examples are orchids (calli on the claw, keeled, semiterete). The labellum is a petal, and a petal claw maps to petal base (rule R2347, as for 'keel claw'). Corolla lips of sympetalous families have no claw, so the orchid reading is safe.

A generic surface pit (of seed coat, pollen exine or fruit surface) that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'pit' and 'areole' (rejected 2026-11-13). The surface is better annotated as a quality of the organ: alveolate, or foveate (PATO_0002296).

target: pedicel (PO_0030112) part of a flower (PO_0009046) qualified female (PATO_0000383), pattern 12; equivalently part of pistillate flower (PO_0025599)
reason: This is the pedicel of the female flowers, not a separate structure. It follows the earlier 'male flower pedicel' answer.
A unit of length ('0.08 inch long'). It belongs in fb:unit or 'has value unit' (UO), and the part described is the raceme, legume, etc. of the sentence. Same as 'μm' and 'kg'.

A diminutive of spine that needs the organ it belongs to (the glochidiate spines of a fruit or cupule, the apical spinelet of a segment or tooth). Same as the rejection of 'spinule' (2026-11-14). Glochidiate fruit spines can be handled where the organ is named.

A small wing on an unnamed organ. 'Wing' was rejected as generic (2026-11-13), and the examples ('lateral winglet primordia', 'winglet(s) lateral development') name neither the organ nor a clear structure. Presence of wings on a named organ is the quality winged (FLOPO_0985004).

The class depends on the family, and the examples mix structures. 'Pilose with short free tip', 'oblong' and 'broadly rounded' fit an anther connective appendage (FLOPO_0986073: Asteraceae, Violaceae). 'Cup-shaped' fits a staminal corona (FLOPO_0985022) or pseudostaminode (FLOPO_0986080). Ground it per flora or family, as was done for 'anther crest'.
Narrower: the cavity in the fruit or endocarp that holds a seed is a fruit locule. Length, width, oblong shape and a smooth or ribbed inner wall describe the locule.
Narrower: the claws of a corolla are the narrowed bases of its petals. This is rule R2347 ('petal claw' -> petal base). 'Claw equaling calyx' is a pattern 10 relation on this bearer.

label: cone scale umbo
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0009027 (megasporophyll; PO synonyms cone scale, ovuliferous scale)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a megasporophyll (PO:0009027) of a megasporangiate strobilus (PO:0005032) that is the raised boss on the exposed part of the scale: terminal or dorsal, flat, raised or depressed, armed with a prickle or unarmed.
reason: A real structure used throughout the conifer floras (Pinus, Cupressaceae) with its own characters: raised, truncate, apiculate, central, unarmed. Bare 'umbo' stays rejected, but with the seed cone named, the organ is fixed. No region pattern (apex, base, margin) expresses it. Propose it to PO beside the cone scale apophysis, which PO also lacks.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of leaf sheath (PO_0020104), pattern 12 (bearer_container PO_0020104)
reason: The summit is the distal end (the mouth) of the sheath, as in Carex and the grasses: U-shaped, V-shaped, truncate, prolonged. It is the apex region of an existing class.

target: synandrium (FLOPO_0986014) in the bearer state sterile (PATO_0000956), pattern 04
reason: In Araceae, a synandrode is a synandrium of staminodes, i.e. a sterile synandrium in the sterile zones of the spadix. Both the synandrium class and PATO sterile exist, so no new term is needed. Shape (depressed, broadly oblong, flat-topped), colour and size are qualities of it.

target: laminal cell (FLOPO_0986100) with has position median (FLOPO_0991381) and upper/distal (FLOPO_0991376), pattern 18; one record per position
reason: Moss leaf cells of the middle and upper lamina. 'Medial and distal' is a conjunction: the measurement holds for both, so it becomes two records, not a union. The laminal cell class exists.
Narrower or near-exact: the axis that bears the flowers. Length, internodes ('entre-noeuds ± 1 mm') and compact or elongated habit describe the inflorescence axis. 'Young' is a pattern 04 state.

target: petal base (PO_0025146) part of wing petal (PO_0025325), bearer_container PO_0025325
reason: Narrower: the claw of a papilionoid wing petal. Same as the earlier 'keel claw' answer and rule R2347.

This comes from French 'folioles' (leaflets); botanical_terminology already gives foliole closeMatch PO_0020049. Length, width, asymmetric and falciform are leaflet qualities. '3-7 paires' is a count of leaflet pairs ('has member', as in pairs of leaflets), not of single leaflets.

Narrower: a leaflet of the third order of a tripinnate leaf or frond. PO does not split leaflets by order, and FLOPO has only pinna (FLOPO_0985027) and pinnule (FLOPO_0985028). Present/absent is pattern 15, and 'deeply lobed' is a leaflet quality.
A generic margin that needs its organ ('inner edge rarely dentate'). Same as the rejection of 'margin' (2026-11-13).

target: gametophore (PO_0030018) in moss floras; stem (PO_0009047) in vascular-plant floras
reason: Narrower in both readings. The examples are mainly moss descriptions: 'julaceous' and 'complanate-foliate' describe the leafy gametophore as a whole, stem and leaves together, so gametophore is the right bearer rather than gametophore stem (PO_0030022). In vascular-plant floras it is the leaf-bearing stem. Use the moss-description switch (by family or moss-only words) to choose.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of involucre (PO_0009100), pattern 12 (bearer_container PO_0009100)
reason: The base region of an existing class (Asteraceae heads: base truncate, rounded, obconic). It parallels the earlier 'involucre margin' answer.
Exact: the class exists. Length, diameter and cylindric shape are its qualities.

target: plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part of calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005), bearer_container FLOPO_0986005
reason: A calyx tooth is a calyx lobe, and its margin (ciliate, narrowly membranous) is the margin region of that class. It follows the earlier 'fruit margin' and 'ligule margin' answers.

Narrower: in Hymenophyllaceae the tubular or bivalved 'involucre' around the sorus is its indusium (conic, not flaring at the mouth, terminal on segments). Do not map it to involucre (PO_0009100), which is a whorl of bracts.
